SELECTED_INDEX: 5
CONFIDENCE: 0.34
EXPLANATION: The dominant Raman band at 2120 cm⁻¹ fits well with a terminal C≡C stretch (typical 2100-2140 cm⁻¹); nitrile stretches (≈2220-2260 cm⁻¹) expected for candidates 2,3,4,6,8,9,10 are not observed, disfavoring those molecules.  
Candidate 5 (C#CC(C)(O)C(C)C) is the only molecule that contains a terminal alkyne but no nitrile, matching the 2120 cm⁻¹ band. Its three methyl groups rationalise the strong C–H stretches at 2896, 2947 and 2989 cm⁻¹ and the CH₃ deformations/rocking at 1455 cm⁻¹ and 716 cm⁻¹ (GFQ-003). The 1003 cm⁻¹ peak corresponds to CH₃ rocking, while the 1058 cm⁻¹ band is consistent with a C–O stretch of the tertiary alcohol. No Si–H, P–H or S=O characteristic bands appear, excluding candidates with Si–H (1), P-containing (7, 10) or sulfoxide (8) functionalities. Thus candidate 5 best matches the observed Raman features.
